title: Norite Gateway Events
description: Source of truth for every frame on the WebSocket at /gateway (docs/architecture.md §2). Updated in the same commit as any new op-code, close code or dispatch type (CLAUDE.md rule 6). backend/gatewayproto is its Go form, and the gateway's tests validate every frame the server sends against this document. Every frame carries op, d, s and t; s and t are null except on a dispatch (op 0).

ClientFrame.description: What a client sends. Ops 3 (presence, M38), 4 (voice state, Phase E) and 8 (member requests) are reserved: sending one closes the connection with 4001, rather than being ignored.

Hello.description: op 10, sent by the server immediately on connect.

version.description: The server's release version, or "dev" for an unstamped build. Compared with the client's under ADR 0033; a dev build on either side is compatible with anything.

HeartbeatAck.description: op 11, the answer to every heartbeat.

Reconnect.description: op 7: the server is going away (a shutdown or a rollout). The connection is then closed with 1012; reconnect and RESUME.

InvalidSession.description: op 9: a RESUME that cannot be honoured. IDENTIFY afresh on the same connection.

d.description: Whether the session may be resumed. false: IDENTIFY afresh.

Dispatch.description: op 0: an event. s is the connection's sequence number, t the event's name.

ReadyDispatch.description: The first dispatch on a new session.

Ready.description: A summary per guild and nothing bulk: channels, roles and member lists are fetched when a guild is opened (lazy per-guild loading, M18). dm_channels and presences are absent until M57 and M38 fill them.

session_id.description: Opaque; RESUME names it, together with the token.

d.description: The last sequence number the client received, or null.

Identify.description: op 2, the first frame a client sends after HELLO.

token.description: An access token. An API token is refused, as is a token whose session has been signed out (close 4004).

intents.description: Reserved; absent or 0 until a milestone defines a bit (close 4013).

Resume.description: op 6, continuing a session after a disconnect: the token again, the session id, and the last sequence number received. Answered by every missed frame in order and then RESUMED; by op 9 false when the session is unknown, expired, somebody else's or too far behind to replay; and by close 4007 for a sequence number the server never sent.

token.description: The access token again: the session id alone would let anybody who read one resume somebody else's stream.

CloseCode.description: Every WebSocket close code the gateway uses after the upgrade.

oneOf.description: Service restart: the server is going away. Sent after op 7; reconnect.
A frame that is not valid gateway JSON, or a payload with unknown fields.
An op other than heartbeat, IDENTIFY or RESUME before IDENTIFY.
Authentication failed: an invalid token, an API token, or a signed-out session. Sign in again.
IDENTIFY or RESUME on a connection that is already identified.
RESUME with a sequence number the server cannot honour.
Rate limited: too many frames, too many IDENTIFYs, or too many connections for one account.
Session timed out: no IDENTIFY, or no heartbeat, in time.
Version mismatch under ADR 0033; the reason names the side to upgrade.
The session was revoked (a sign-out, a password reset, a ban). Sign in again.
The client did not read fast enough and its outbound buffer filled. Reconnect and resync.

Snowflake.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Snowflake; a test holds the two equal. A Snowflake ID as a decimal string. Always a string, never a JSON number — Snowflakes exceed 2^53, so numeric parsing silently loses precision (docs/adr/0003-snowflake-ids.md).

User.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/User; a test holds the two equal. An account. Never carries `password_hash` or any other credential material — this shape is built field-by-field from the database row rather than serialised from it, so a column added later cannot leak onto the wire by default.

email_verified_at.description: Null while the address is unconfirmed. Set when a confirmation link is followed (M10), when a provider vouched for the address, or on creation for an account made by `/instance/bootstrap` or on an instance with no mail relay. An account with this null cannot sign in.

two_factor_enabled.description: True only for a *confirmed* enrollment. An enrollment somebody started and abandoned is not a factor and must not read as one, or the account looks protected when it is not.

recovery_codes_remaining.description: How many unspent recovery codes the account has. Null rather than zero when there is no factor at all — zero would read as "you have run out" rather than "there is nothing to run out of".

owner_id.description: The account that bypasses every permission check within this guild (authority layer 2). Cannot be removed from the guild; the owner hands it on with `POST /guilds/{guild_id}/owner`.

icon_hash.description: Reserved. No upload endpoint exists yet, so this is always null.

message_audit_enabled.description:
Whether this guild records every message its members send to a log its moderators can read (M16b), including edits and deletions. Off unless the guild's owner turned it on.

**Readable by any member**, deliberately: this endpoint requires membership and nothing else, so being told whether you are recorded does not depend on holding a permission. Reading the log itself needs `VIEW_MESSAGE_AUDIT` and writing this field needs the owner; neither is required to learn the answer.

Always present, in both states. A client must be able to say "this guild does not record" as positively as it says the opposite — a field that appeared only when recording was on would make its absence carry a meaning nothing guarantees.

Guild.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Guild; a test holds the two equal.

permission_overwrites.description:
Every overwrite configured on this channel — as configured, not as resolved for the caller.

Required and never null, on every route that returns a channel. An omitted array and an empty one would be one schema meaning two things depending on which route produced it, and a client refreshing its cache from a response is entitled to read this as the whole truth.

Present on the listing because a permission editor cannot be drawn without it and there is no single-channel `GET` to ask instead. The listing already reads every channel in the guild, so one further query answers the whole sidebar rather than one request per tab opened.

guild_id.description: Null for a DM or group DM, which belong to no guild.

type.description:
`0` text, `1` DM, `2` voice, `3` group DM, `4` category, `5` announcement (reserved), `6` stage voice (reserved), `7` public matchmaking.

Only `0`, `2` and `4` can be created through the guild-channel endpoint. The reserved values are part of the schema and stay there; voice is active v1 functionality, video and stage voice are the deferred-but-seamed parts.

parent_id.description: The category this channel sits under. Deleting a category sets this to null on its children rather than deleting them — losing a category must not lose the conversations in it.

last_message_id.description:
The newest message in the channel, or null if none has been sent. Maintained in the send's own transaction (M15) rather than derived with `max(id)` on every channel listing, which would be an N+1 across the sidebar.

**View-gated, not history-gated.** It is returned to anyone who can see the channel, including a member denied `READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY` — it is the unread-state primitive, and a client cannot render an unread marker without it. What that discloses is a snowflake, and therefore a timestamp: that somebody posted, and when. The content stays withheld. Discord exposes the same field under the same conditions. Recorded as a decision because it reads like an oversight otherwise.

bitrate.description: Voice channels only; null on every other type.

user_limit.description: Voice channels only; null on every other type.

Channel.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Channel; a test holds the two equal.

color.description: 24-bit RGB. `0` means no colour, which renders as inherited rather than as black.

position.description: Higher is higher in the hierarchy. `@everyone` is always 0. Not settable through these endpoints — reordering is a multi-row operation, and role hierarchy arrives with the permission-overwrite endpoints.

hoist.description: Whether members holding this role are shown in their own section of the member list.

is_default.description: True for exactly one role per guild, `@everyone`. It is the floor every other role stacks on, it cannot be deleted or renamed, and every member holds it without appearing in any grant.

Role.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Role; a test holds the two equal.

nickname.description: A per-guild display name. Null means the account's own display name is used.

deaf.description: Server-side deafen, set by a moderator. Distinct from the self-deafen a client sets on itself, which lives in voice state.

mute.description: Server-side mute, set by a moderator. See `deaf`.

roles.description: The roles this member holds, excluding `@everyone` — which every member holds and which appears in no grant. An empty array rather than null when there are none: a client that has to handle both writes the check once per field and forgets it somewhere.

Member.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Member; a test holds the two equal.

PublicUser.description: The part of an account other people see (M20a): a message's author, an invite's issuer. A username is a public handle and the display name is what the account chose to be shown as; never the email. Not carried by GUILD_MEMBER_ADD, which is a Member: no REST read returns another member's name.

author_id.description: Null for a message with no author — a system or webhook message. Never null because the author's account was deleted: a deleted account is soft-deleted and its messages survive attributed to it, which is what `messages.author_id` carrying no `ON DELETE` guarantees.

author.description: Who wrote it. Null when `author_id` is null, and null when the author's account was deleted, where `author_id` survives: a client renders the second as a deleted account, and never shows the placeholder name a deleted account is renamed to.

type.description: 0 default, 1 sent via automation (webhooks, bot automation). Higher values reserved.

tags.description:
The tags on the message this caller can see: every shared tag, plus the caller's own private ones. Somebody else's private tag never appears.

**Null when the credential may not read tags** — an API token without the `tags.read` scope. Null rather than an empty array, because an empty array would claim the message has no tags when the answer is that they are not this credential's to see. A signed-in user always gets an array, empty for an untagged message.

The channel listing resolves a whole page's tags at once, so a client drawing a channel needs no per-message request; `GET /channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/tags` remains for reading one message's tags on their own.

Message.description: Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Message; a test holds the two equal.

PermissionOverwrite.description:
Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/PermissionOverwrite; a test holds the two equal. One channel permission overwrite — ADR 0008 layer 5.

`target_id` is polymorphic: a role id when `type` is 0, a user id when it is 1. It carries no foreign key for that reason, which is why deleting a role or removing a member deletes their overwrites explicitly rather than leaving the database to cascade.

Permissions.description:
Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Permissions; a test holds the two equal. A permission bitfield, as a **decimal string** rather than a number.

The same decision snowflake ids take, for the same reason: this is a 63-bit value and JavaScript's number type is a float64, so anything above 2^53 loses precision silently in a browser. Twenty-two bits are defined today, so the hazard is years away — which is exactly why the representation is fixed now, while changing it costs nothing.

Bit positions, low to high: `VIEW_CHANNEL`, `SEND_MESSAGES`, `MANAGE_MESSAGES`, `MANAGE_CHANNELS`, `MANAGE_ROLES`, `KICK_MEMBERS`, `BAN_MEMBERS`, `CREATE_INVITE`, `MANAGE_GUILD`, `ADMINISTRATOR`, `CONNECT_VOICE`, `SPEAK_VOICE`, `VIDEO_VOICE`, `MUTE_MEMBERS`, `DEAFEN_MEMBERS`, `MENTION_EVERYONE`, `MANAGE_WEBHOOKS`, `MANAGE_EMOJIS`, `MODERATE_MEMBERS`, `VIEW_AUDIT_LOG`, `READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY`, `VIEW_MESSAGE_AUDIT`.

**The order is data, not documentation.** What the database stores is bit positions, so renumbering reassigns every permission every guild has already granted. `VIDEO_VOICE` is reserved and granted by nothing; it is listed because removing it would renumber the six bits above it.

AppliedMessageTag.description:
Generated from contracts/openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/AppliedMessageTag; a test holds the two equal. A tag as it appears on a message — the tag itself, plus who put it there and when.

`applied_by` is present deliberately. A tag on a message is an assertion somebody made about it, and a reader deciding whether to trust `spam` wants to know who said so, the same reason an audit entry names an actor. It discloses nothing: everybody named here is a member of a guild the reader is also in.

GuildDeleted.description: GUILD_DELETE: the guild is gone, or this account is no longer in it. The client drops it either way.

ChannelDeleted.description: CHANNEL_DELETE, sent only to members who could view the channel.

GuildRoles.description: GUILD_ROLES_UPDATE: the guild`s whole role list, which the client replaces. Whole because creating or reordering one role moves the others.

MemberRemoved.description: GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE, to the members who remain.

PermissionsUpdated.description: GUILD_PERMISSIONS_UPDATE: which channels you may see, or what you may do, may have changed. Refetch the guild`s channels.

MessageDeleted.description: MESSAGE_DELETE, to members who can view the channel.

GuildCreateDispatch.description: To an account that has just come into the guild — the account that created it, or since M20a one that joined it through an invite — adding the guild to its connections. Not a statement that the recipient created it: compare owner_id.

GuildUpdateDispatch.description: To members, including after an ownership transfer.

GuildDeleteDispatch.description: To members of a deleted guild, and to an account removed from one.

ChannelCreateDispatch.description: To members who can view the new channel.

ChannelUpdateDispatch.description: To members who can view the channel.

ChannelDeleteDispatch.description: To members who could view the channel.

GuildRolesUpdateDispatch.description: To members, after any role is created, edited, deleted or reordered.

GuildMemberAddDispatch.description: To members, after somebody joins through an invite (M20a). A Member and not the joiner's name: no REST read returns another member's name, and the gateway never discloses more than REST. The joiner receives it too, after the GUILD_CREATE that adds the guild to their connection.

GuildMemberUpdateDispatch.description: To members, after a member is edited or given or relieved of a role.

GuildPermissionsUpdateDispatch.description: To members, after anything that can change what they may see or do.

MessageCreateDispatch.description: To members who can view the channel. tags is always null on the gateway: private tags differ per reader, so they are read over REST.

MessageUpdateDispatch.description: To members who can view the channel. tags is always null, as for MESSAGE_CREATE.

MessageDeleteDispatch.description: To members who can view the channel.

Resumed.description: RESUMED's payload is empty: its sequence number, after every replayed frame, is the message.

ResumedDispatch.description: Sent after a RESUME has replayed every frame the client missed, in order. Events that arrive after it are live.
